regions.full_page: I was pleased to receive your kind favor of the 9th even though it was not as bright, as of course, we all would like to see it. However, God knows best, and, while we'll still hope for a favorable surprise, we can hardly do better than, not only be resigned to whatever God permits, but even beforehand thank Him for His mercifully loving designs. In this way we can foster confidence in God, whis is the very soul of prayer, and con- sequently heighten our hopes for supernatural int- ervention. Not only this, but in thus fostering confidence, we greatly eliminate the danger of sadness, want of resignation and impatience which, though not necessarily sinful in themselves, never- theless sadly frustrate God's merciful designs. Hence the little verse: "God condescerds to use our powers If we don't spoil His plans by ours." Besides this, dear Mr. Morgan; I want to thank you for your practical interest in the apalling cas of Dr. Kraus; whose efforts and personal sacrafices in the cause of the very principles of justice and truth -- of religion as against atheism, the supreme science of our hanny relationship with God and our neighbor against the "diabolical climax of intel- lectual and spiritual insanity -- has been so out- standing and, at times, so internationally recognized.
